articles.title: SaaS Metrics for Developers: MRR, Churn, LTV:CAC and Runway, With the Math in Code
articles.excerpt: Your side project has paying users. Stripe shows a balance, a chart that mostly goes up, and a list of payments. Then someone asks for your MRR, your churn or your LTV:CAC, and the dashboard doesn't q…
articles.body: Your side project has paying users. Stripe shows a balance, a chart that mostly goes up, and a list of payments. Then someone asks for your MRR, your churn or your LTV:CAC, and the dashboard doesn't quite answer. Most of these metrics are a line or two of arithmetic. What makes them confusing is the definitions: what counts as recurring, which churn, revenue or profit. Get those wrong and the numbers look healthier than the business is. We explain each one in the StartupReader learn section and built free calculators for them. This post puts them in one place for developers, each as a few lines of JavaScript you can paste into a console and run against your own numbers. The examples use round, made-up numbers for a small subscription product.

articles.title: Stop Rebuilding the Same Firmware: Turning One-Off IoT Projects Into Reusable Assets
articles.excerpt: I used to think the hardest part of an embedded project was getting the board to boot. It isn't. The hardest part is what happens after you hand it over. For years I built commercial IoT projects on E…
articles.body: I used to think the hardest part of an embedded project was getting the board to boot. It isn't. The hardest part is what happens after you hand it over. For years I built commercial IoT projects on Espressif modules — ESP32 mostly, occasionally an ESP8266 when the BOM was tight. Sensor nodes, controller boxes, gateway firmware, the usual. They all followed the same arc: a few weeks of late nights fighting a flaky I2C bus or a modem that wouldn't reconnect, a demo that finally worked, final payment, and then silence. The code went into a folder named after the client. Six months later another client would ask for something 80% similar, and I'd start from scratch anyway, because the old code was so welded to that one job that untangling it took longer than rewriting.
articles.author: Kevin Lee

articles.title: Self-Hosting Listmonk on Railway: The Newsletter Server That Can't Send Email on the Wrong Plan
articles.excerpt: Listmonk is an open-source newsletter and mailing-list manager: subscriber lists, segmentation with SQL, campaign templates, analytics, and transactional mail over an API. It's a single Go binary back…
articles.body: Listmonk is an open-source newsletter and mailing-list manager: subscriber lists, segmentation with SQL, campaign templates, analytics, and transactional mail over an API. It's a single Go binary backed by Postgres, it idles at a few tens of megabytes of RAM, and it's free — the only per-email cost is whichever mail provider actually delivers your messages. That combination makes it one of the cheapest things you can self-host. It also means the things that go wrong are not "it crashed" but "it's running and nothing is being delivered", which is worse. This guide covers running Listmonk on Railway, a usage-billed container platform with managed Postgres and volumes. Most of it applies to any container host. How Listmonk sends mail Listmonk doesn't deliver email itself.

articles.title: An APX Interface Should Ask the Daemon, Not a Plugin
articles.excerpt: An APX Interface Should Ask the Daemon, Not a Plugin A new APX interface should not learn how to manage plugins. It should ask the daemon. That sounds like an implementation detail, but it is a bounda…
articles.body: An APX Interface Should Ask the Daemon, Not a Plugin A new APX interface should not learn how to manage plugins. It should ask the daemon. That sounds like an implementation detail, but it is a boundary that keeps agent behavior coherent as APX gains surfaces. APC is the portable context layer. A repository can carry AGENTS.md , .apc/agents/ , skills, and other durable project rules. APX is the daily-use runtime and tooling layer: it reads that context, runs agent work locally, and exposes it through a CLI, web panel, desktop client, and other interfaces. The important split inside APX is just as deliberate. The architecture documents three layers: core/ for shared logic, host/ for long-running processes, and interfaces/ for surfaces. The daemon lives in host/ .

articles.excerpt: Abstract Problem Statement System Architecture Inference Layer: Groq API running high-throughput Llama-based models with automated dynamic fallback error handling. Memory Layer: Vectorize Hindsight Cl…
articles.body: Abstract Enterprise B2B sales interactions involve long multi-month negotiation windows where critical deal context gets lost in manual CRM updates. Standard Large Language Models (LLMs) operate statelessly, resetting memory context after every session. This article details the architecture of Omni Deal Intelligence, a solution integrating Groq's high-speed LLM inference engine with Vectorize Hindsight's persistent episodic memory architecture. Problem Statement Sales representatives lose an average of 12–15 hours weekly manually transcribing call notes, tracking past objections, and reconciling previous commitments. When context slips, deals stall or fail completely during executive procurement reviews.

articles.body: Credit: Robert Triggs / Android Authority I’ve been cruising in Google’s free storage tier for as long as I can remember, backing up my Photos, emails, and even WhatsApp messages without ever spending a penny. But over the past few months, I’ve been creeping up to the 15GB cap (17GB in my case , as an old-timer who jumped through Google’s security hoops), leading to a barrage of Google One notifications urging me to upgrade to a paid storage tier. That’s never going to happen. The economics of starting out at just $1.99 a month for 100GB might not sound like much, but I know it won’t be many more years before I hit that limit, too. Then I’d be hooked: forking out $4.99 and then $9.99 every month, in perpetuity, for the luxury of having Google back up my odds and ends.

articles.title: 4-billion-year-old 'Rosetta Stone' found in Sahara Desert could unlock the secret history of water on Mars
articles.excerpt: A rock discovered in the Sahara Desert formed more than 4.1 billion years ago, making it one of the oldest Martian meteorites ever found. The ancient space rock offers a rare glimpse into the formatio…
articles.body: A rose-colored rock discovered in the Sahara Desert may hold some clues to Mars' ancient geological history. The meteorite , named Teghaza 001 after the salt plain in Mali where it was discovered in 2022, weighs roughly 1.8 pounds (800 grams) and formed more than 4.1 billion years ago. Blasted off Mars by an impact before eventually landing on Earth, it is one of the three oldest Martian meteorites ever found. The extraordinary age and unusual mineral composition of Teghaza 001 offer a rare glimpse into the formation of Mars' early crust and how volcanic materials may have been altered by water, according to a statement from NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California.

The onboard AI is claimed to predict your next steps and take action automatically, such as ordering an Uber only after you finish breakfast. It’s available for pre-ordering and will start shipping early next year. Smart rings have lately been seen as viable alternatives to smartwatches because of their non-existent footprint, which makes them easier to wear all day. articles.body: Perplexity is taking on OpenAI and Anthropic with its own work-focused AI agents. The startup's new always-on "Teammates" can take on multiple roles within a workspace, while pulling existing projects, skills, and memory from the Perplexity tools you already use. Teammates integrate with Perplexity Computer , an AI system that can deploy agents on your device to complete tasks. articles.title: 'We got it done!' Spacewalking astronauts finish installing next-gen ISS solar arrays
articles.excerpt: Spacewalkers Anil Menon and Joshua Kutryk installed the final ISS Roll-Out Solar Array on Thursday (Nov. 5), wrapping up a multiyear effort to boost the station's power generation by 30%.
articles.body: Just as NASA is preparing to demonstrate " Max Power " on the ground, two astronauts on a spacewalk have provided the International Space Station (ISS) with the same. Expedition 75 flight engineers Anil Menon of NASA and Joshua Kutryk of the Canadian Space Agency installed and deployed the eighth and final ISS Roll-Out Solar Array (iROSA) on Thursday (Nov. 5), augmenting the space station's legacy solar array wings to produce as much as 30% more electricity. "We got it done!" said Menon at the end of the 6-hour-and-59-minute spacewalk . The EVA (extravehicular activity) began at 8:36 a.m. EST and ended at 3:35 p.m. EST (1336 to 2035 GMT).

articles.title: Andy Weir says his new sci-fi audio drama 'Exoplanet' is a way to 'revive the old art of radio plays' (interview)
articles.excerpt: "Earlier on in my life, even before 'The Martian,' I wanted to bring back audio-only entertainment."
articles.body: Hot off the tremendous theatrical success of this year's "Project Hail Mary," adapted from Andy Weir's 2021 novel of the same name, the New York Times bestselling author is rocketing back into deep space with a brand new Audible Original release landing on Nov. 5, 2026, titled " Exoplanet ." Weir (" The Martian ") is executive producing this ambitious full-cast audiobook drama with acclaimed author and ace comic writer Benjamin Percy ("Wolverine") for the first in a series of curated sci-fi projects for Amazon's Audible. The seven-episode sci-fi thriller stars the vocal talents of Anthony Mackie, Ariana DeBose, and John Leguizamo in a wild time-travel space disaster odyssey that also benefits from Lucasfilm’s Skywalker Sound, which provided the show’s immersive acoustic elements.
